articles.title: The case of the spiky file descriptors
articles.read_scope: Complete substantive prose and code excerpts; charts not independently measured.

practice.trigger: A proxy migration leaves periodic connection or goroutine growth.
practice.failure: Retired certificate ownership still admits requests that queue behind slow certificate acquisition.
practice.mechanism: Correlate individual socket lifetimes, logs, goroutine stacks, and the owning configuration before changing limits.
practice.conditions: The old endpoint remains reachable and certificate provisioning follows the reported Go autocert path.
practice.counterexample: A traffic-driven increase is not automatically a leak; cached certificates also bypass the new-certificate HostPolicy.
practice.verification: With an empty cache, verify HostPolicy denies new certificate acquisition and resource counts remain bounded. If retiring endpoint access is required, add a separate routing or host-access policy and test that policy with both empty and warm caches.

articles.limitations: Historical incident; hardcoded client DNS and certificate-expiry trigger were author hypotheses, not proven facts. Current autocert documentation qualifies HostPolicy scope.

articles.title: Continuously fuzzing Python C extensions
articles.access: public HTML through web reader; direct urllib returned 403
articles.read_scope: Complete substantive prose, harness, build discussion, crash diagnosis, OSS-Fuzz and CI sections.

practice.trigger: Untrusted bytes cross a Python parser or decoder implemented in a native extension.
practice.failure: Python-level checks miss memory errors in the actual native implementation.
practice.mechanism: Confirm the native import and sanitizer instrumentation, fuzz in a reproducible environment, and retain replayable crash inputs.
practice.conditions: Compiler, sanitizer, runtime, and extension build must be compatible.
practice.counterexample: The article suppresses Python exceptions to target memory corruption; copying that policy into a logic-fuzzing harness hides failures.
practice.verification: Replay a known failure under the same pinned build, then verify the fix and retained regression.

articles.limitations: Historical cbor2 example; not a claim about current vulnerability. Linux preload instructions are not portable unchanged to macOS. Leak detection was deliberately disabled.

articles.title: I wrote a 70x faster SQL parser while barely looking at the code
articles.read_scope: Complete substantive article, including motivation, two implementations, generation, shrinking, regression loop, and shadow rollout.

practice.trigger: Replace an implementation while preserving an established behavioral contract.
practice.failure: Agent fixes overfit individual examples or lose authoritative grammar context.
practice.mechanism: Compare with an explicit oracle, generate structured inputs, shrink discrepancies, retain regressions, and reload the relevant specification before fixing.
practice.conditions: Oracle behavior and permitted differences are decided; shadow execution is safe for the target.
practice.counterexample: An oracle may preserve a bug; production-corpus agreement does not prove all-input equivalence.
practice.verification: Run retained counterexamples and independent input families; distinguish measured speed from correctness evidence.

articles.limitations: Author-reported performance and production outcomes were not independently reproduced. Pure-parser shadow execution does not authorize duplicating real side effects.

articles.title: Slow and Steady: Converting Sentry’s Entire Frontend to TypeScript
articles.read_scope: Complete substantive prose and code examples; progress-chart values not independently extracted.

practice.trigger: A large JavaScript codebase accumulates type-related defects while product work continues.
practice.failure: A broad conversion combines incompatible refactors or treats a typed filename as verified safety.
practice.mechanism: Migrate bounded dependency slices, verify imported declarations, and track unresolved typing decisions explicitly.
practice.conditions: Mixed JavaScript and TypeScript remain supported during migration; delivery constraints permit incremental adoption.
practice.counterexample: Type assertions and annotations do not validate network input; historical React workarounds may be obsolete.
practice.verification: Run the actual compiler and behavioral tests, and test malformed runtime inputs at trust boundaries.

articles.limitations: Frontend case study; application to backend migration is an inference. Claimed organizational benefits are observational, not controlled causal evidence.
